All other 7-9 candidates still received Deep Source Review; narrative non-selection does not reduce evidence depth.

full_source_reviews.title: Action-Conditioned World Model for Goal Plane Probe Guidance in Robotic Ultrasound

locators.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 does not disclose a public executable artifact; no code or dataset behavior claim is retained

full_source_reviews.mechanism_summary: A frozen action-conditioned latent transition model becomes a reward-bearing component of a bounded perception-action loop; real observation remains the authority after every action.
full_source_reviews.analysis_old: Direct imitation and visual servoing remain rational with dense targets and feedback; explicit simulation remains rational when image physics is tractable.
full_source_reviews.analysis_tradeoff: Learned transition rewards reduce expert-label pressure but import model bias and diffusion cost; bounded real feedback and an external safety envelope must remain authoritative.
full_source_reviews.problem_and_old_solution: Direct imitation, visual servoing and explicit simulators were reasonable when expert trajectories or tractable image physics were available, but ultrasound contact, deformation and acoustic artifacts make both expensive and brittle.
full_source_reviews.mechanism_and_state: A latent conditional diffusion model owns predicted future ultrasound state conditioned on recent frames, 6-DoF relative motion and time offset. A goal-conditioned temporal actor owns action/stop decisions; the frozen world model supplies a perceptual progress reward against a multi-sample goal-plane bank.
full_source_reviews.control_and_data_flow: image/action trajectories -> VAE latents -> conditional denoising rollout -> predicted future latent -> goal-distance reward -> actor-critic fine-tuning -> real robot executes one bounded action -> observation closes the loop.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: Self-collected neck-ultrasound data; carotid and thyroid protocols; offline future-frame/action evaluation plus real-world closed-loop success. Model, robot/probe setup, subject count and trajectory construction are paper-specific; throughput, hardware precision, concurrency and serving SLO are not disclosed.
full_source_reviews.proved: The paper supports that learned action-conditioned acoustic dynamics can improve this specific goal-plane policy and reports 70.0% carotid and 65.0% thyroid success in its own closed-loop setup.
full_source_reviews.not_proved: It does not establish patient-independent clinical safety, broad anatomy transfer, calibrated rollout uncertainty, or superiority to all direct policies and physics simulators.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_failure_coexistence: Synthetic rollouts reduce expert-label pressure but import model bias into reward; diffusion adds iterative cost; the goal bank and single-axis bins bound control but constrain maneuver expressivity. Direct visual servoing remains preferable when targets are easy and feedback dense; explicit simulation remains useful where physics is reliable.

full_source_reviews.title: RIS-Kernel: A Model-Agnostic Architecture for Long-Context LLM Inference via Sparse Attention
full_source_reviews.source_route: exact v1 HTML; paper links code, Zenodo data and Code Ocean capsule

locators.artifact: https://github.com/santosardr/riskernel — repository disclosed by exact v1; https://doi.org/10.24433/CO.0351350.v1 — Code Ocean capsule disclosed by exact v1; neither artifact was executed and an immutable event-time commit was not audited

full_source_reviews.mechanism_summary: RIS combines cached stochastic global anchors, a recent local window and dynamic positional scaling as an experimental sparse-attention branch whose coverage and extrapolation errors remain distinct.
full_source_reviews.analysis_old: Dense attention remains exact when it fits; deterministic local/global sparse patterns remain cheaper and easier to reason about when stochastic coverage is unacceptable.
full_source_reviews.analysis_tradeoff: More anchors and seeds raise recall but multiply work and memory; positional extrapolation and quadratic mask construction remain separate limits.
full_source_reviews.problem_and_old_solution: Dense attention is exact within the trained window but quadratic; fixed local windows are cheap but can miss distal anchors. RIS samples sparse global geometry and ensembles seeds to recover coverage.
full_source_reviews.mechanism_and_state: A cached stochastic anchor plus a dynamic recent window determines attended indices; PFUS normalizes their union once; dynamic RoPE scaling handles extrapolated positions without changing weights.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct and TinyLlama-1.1B on author-built 32-question/64-question scientific retrieval tasks; 32k dense comparison and 64k extrapolation; CPU i7-3770 16GB and dual-socket Xeon 128GB; Float32; ensemble/density varied. Output length, batch, concurrency and latency SLO are not disclosed.
full_source_reviews.proved: Within this small benchmark, selected density/seed settings match or exceed the dense accuracy point and permit 64k execution where the chosen dense implementation OOMs.
full_source_reviews.not_proved: The evaluation does not validate quality across modern large models, standard long-context suites, GPU kernels, general generation, or production latency. The paper's own geometry construction still discusses O(N^2) boolean allocation, so the O(N log N) headline must not be generalized to total memory/runtime without implementation qualification.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_failure_coexistence: More seeds improve coverage but multiply work and memory; high density reintroduces distractors; extrapolation remains bounded by positional encoding. Dense/FlashAttention remains the correctness and throughput baseline when it fits; deterministic sparse patterns remain attractive when stochastic variance is unacceptable.
full_source_reviews.evidence_level: Primary experimental preprint with public artifacts

full_source_reviews.title: Ground Truth First: A Longitudinal Evaluation Instrument for Agent Memory, and the Tenure Crossover in Memory-Architecture Rankings

locators.artifact: https://github.com/veracium-ai/Veracium — repository disclosed by exact v1; event-time immutable commit and executable behavior were not audited

full_source_reviews.mechanism_summary: Ground-truth facts, validity intervals, provenance and as-of dates become canonical state before conversation rendering, enabling separate write/read audits and tenure-aware architecture comparison.
full_source_reviews.analysis_old: Conversation-first short-horizon sets are cheap and remain useful smoke tests; full history is a valid small-tenure reference when token pressure has not arrived.
full_source_reviews.analysis_tradeoff: Truth-first construction improves auditability and reveals tenure crossover, but uses synthetic users and adds provenance/version-control obligations; accuracy still does not prove cautious behavior.
full_source_reviews.problem_and_old_solution: Conversation-first memory benchmarks are easy to generate but can contain label errors, contamination and histories too short to reveal retention pressure. The new instrument generates immutable facts and validity intervals before rendering conversations.
full_source_reviews.mechanism_and_state: Ground-truth facts, temporal validity, provenance and question-as-of dates are the canonical state; conversation text is a derived view. Five memory architectures plus full-history/no-memory controls are replayed at multiple tenures with stochastic replication and separate read/write audits.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: Six nine-week users plus short-horizon users, multiple question types and three stochastic replicates; five engineered memory architectures, full-history and no-memory controls; judge-based and judge-independent checks. The corpus is synthetic/scripted and architecture/backbone choices remain bounded to the released harness.
full_source_reviews.proved: The instrument demonstrates that short histories can obscure architecture differences and that rankings change after early facts are evicted; at week nine the layered system and full history have no judge-independent accuracy winner while their token growth differs sharply.
full_source_reviews.not_proved: It does not show one universal memory architecture, production-user validity, or that benchmark accuracy guarantees cautious behavior; the paper explicitly observes that accuracy does not confer caution.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_failure_coexistence: Ground-truth-first construction gains auditability but loses some natural human interaction complexity. Full history stays a valid reference for small histories; structured memory becomes valuable under tenure/token pressure but introduces write-path extraction and mutation failure modes.

full_source_reviews.title: Unified Static-Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
full_source_reviews.source_route: exact v1 HTML; official GitHub artifact linked in paper

locators.artifact: https://github.com/AIDASLab/SPDP — official repository disclosed by exact v1; event-time immutable commit and executable behavior were not audited

full_source_reviews.mechanism_summary: Static weight sparsity and input-dependent activation sparsity become composable through a shared column-addressable representation with phase-specific decode and prefill kernels.
full_source_reviews.analysis_old: Static pruning is stable and bandwidth-saving; dynamic pruning adapts per input; dense or structured kernels remain strong when arithmetic intensity and portability dominate.
full_source_reviews.analysis_tradeoff: Joint sparsity raises effective zeros but pays bitmap metadata, layout specialization and two phase-specific execution paths; prefill and high-batch gains are not guaranteed.
full_source_reviews.problem_and_old_solution: Static weight pruning saves bandwidth but cannot exploit input-dependent activation redundancy; dynamic pruning adapts per token but creates irregular column access. Applying either independently leaves the other sparsity dimension unused.
full_source_reviews.mechanism_and_state: Tiled-CBC stores statically pruned weights in column-addressable microtiles. Decode uses CUDA-core sparse-matrix/sparse-vector execution with activation-aware bitmap decoding; prefill reuses the format through a Tensor-Core SpMM path, avoiding phase-specific reformatting.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: LLaMA-2-7B quality/end-to-end tests and sparse-kernel tests on NVIDIA A10G, L4 and L40S; 10 warmups plus 100 measured executions; mean wall-clock latency; comparisons include SpInfer and cuBLAS. Exact request concurrency and production SLO are not disclosed.
full_source_reviews.proved: Under tested sparsity/quality points SPDP reports 1.24x/1.37x average speedup over SpInfer on A10G/L4, lower TPOT at matched perplexity, and up to 25% more sparsity at comparable perplexity.
full_source_reviews.not_proved: Results do not establish portability to H100-class kernels, other architectures/quantization formats, high-batch serving, or unstructured pruning as universally preferable.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_failure_coexistence: Joint sparsity multiplies opportunity but requires a bespoke representation and two execution paths; metadata/bitmap decoding can erase gains outside memory-bound small-batch decode. Dense Tensor-Core kernels and structured sparsity remain preferable at high arithmetic intensity or where toolchain portability dominates.

full_source_reviews.title: Music-JEPA: Learning a World Model of Sound from Action
full_source_reviews.source_route: exact v1 HTML; demo page accessible from paper, code/pretrained models promised but not yet released in v1

locators.artifact: https://zzwaang.github.io/music-jepa-demo/ — demo disclosed by exact v1; code and checkpoints were only promised for future release, so no executable artifact claim is retained

full_source_reviews.mechanism_summary: An audio JEPA reuses action-conditioned latent transition semantics for controllable sound, but remains an offline piano-domain case already covered by the world-model abstraction.
full_source_reviews.analysis_old: Audio reconstruction and generation remain appropriate when waveform fidelity rather than controllable transition is the objective.
full_source_reviews.analysis_tradeoff: Latent prediction avoids reconstruction cost but weakens waveform interpretability and binds inverse planning to the learned action manifold; exact v1 lacked released code/checkpoints.
full_source_reviews.problem_and_old_solution: Audio representation learning usually predicts or reconstructs observations without an explicit controllable cause. Music-JEPA treats pianoroll as action and audio as state to learn action-conditioned latent transition.
full_source_reviews.mechanism_and_state: The encoder supplies audio state, the action encoder supplies pianoroll action, and a predictor estimates the future target-encoder latent. A separately trained inverse predictor/action decoder performs amortized planning from current and desired sound states.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: Offline paired piano audio-pianoroll data; latent-dynamics diagnostics, music-information-retrieval downstream tasks and transcription/planning experiments. No physical environment interaction; code and checkpoints were not released at v1.
full_source_reviews.proved: The experiments support action-conditioned latent prediction and useful representations within the piano-sound domain.
full_source_reviews.not_proved: They do not demonstrate an interactive environment model, broad audio causality, real-time control, or artifact reproducibility at v1.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_failure_coexistence: Latent prediction avoids waveform reconstruction cost but weakens direct perceptual interpretability; amortized inverse planning scales better than direct gradient search but is tied to the learned action manifold. Generative audio models remain appropriate when waveform fidelity, not controllable transition, is the goal.

full_source_reviews.title: Scaling Native Multimodal Pre-Training From Scratch

locators.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 does not disclose an independently executable training artifact; no code or checkpoint behavior claim is retained

full_source_reviews.mechanism_summary: Native multimodal pretraining turns shared capacity allocation into a multi-objective Pareto decision because text and multimodal losses prefer different parameter and token budgets.
full_source_reviews.analysis_old: Late fusion remains rational for encoder reuse, cheaper upgrades and modality-specific specialization; scalar compute-optimal rules are sufficient only for one objective and one token economy.
full_source_reviews.analysis_tradeoff: Native integration can transfer across modalities but couples budgets and makes allocation Pareto; the fitted exponents remain architecture, data and measurement specific.
full_source_reviews.problem_and_old_solution: Late fusion reuses mature language and vision encoders but inherits modality asymmetry. Native joint pretraining removes that boundary, yet a single Chinchilla-style model/token optimum does not say how shared parameters should serve separate text and multimodal losses.
full_source_reviews.mechanism_and_state: A decoder-only MoE consumes text tokens and continuous image patch embeddings from scratch. Independent IsoFLOP and training-envelope estimators fit text and multimodal objectives, then form a Pareto frontier over shared parameter count, text-token budget and multimodal-token budget.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: 71M-to-3B activated-parameter model family; 250B text tokens and up to 75B multimodal tokens; 4K context; 16 text and 23 multimodal benchmarks, with 21 used for few-shot analysis. Training loss is used as test-loss proxy for scaling fits; hardware, precision and full data provenance are not disclosed in the inspected v1 text.
full_source_reviews.proved: Within this model/data regime, text and multimodal losses prefer different allocations; adding up to 0.3 multimodal-token ratio changes aggregate text accuracy by under one point, improves tested text-only spatial tasks, and yields multimodal in-context learning at larger scales.
full_source_reviews.not_proved: The fitted exponents are not universal laws across architectures, discrete image tokenizers, larger contexts or proprietary corpora; training-loss proxy and undisclosed data/hardware constrain extrapolation.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_failure_coexistence: Native training gains shared representations and cross-modal transfer but couples modality budgets and makes compute allocation multi-objective; late fusion remains rational when pretrained assets, modality specialization or cheap upgrades matter. More multimodal tokens can favor data over parameters and increase ingestion/curation cost.

full_source_reviews.title: Agentic CPU-GPU Scheduling for Heterogeneous AI Workloads

locators.artifact: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.22242v1#A2 — exact-v1 prompt and scheduler example; https://arxiv.org/html/2607.22242v1#A3 — exact-v1 mapping trace; no separately executable artifact is disclosed

full_source_reviews.mechanism_summary: An LLM proposes heterogeneous placement from monitored CPU, immediate-GPU and queued-GPU state, while a deterministic executor retains DAG and memory-feasibility authority.
full_source_reviews.analysis_old: GPU-first is simple; HEFT and classical schedulers remain deterministic and effective under stable profiles and known resource models.
full_source_reviews.analysis_tradeoff: Advisory LLM reasoning can adapt without training but adds latency, nondeterminism, prompt sensitivity and telemetry dependence; deterministic admission must contain those failures.
full_source_reviews.problem_and_old_solution: GPU-first placement is simple when GPU-capable tools uniformly benefit, while HEFT/StarPU are effective with stable profiles. Heterogeneous agent workflows add contention, VRAM admission and data-transfer effects that make static isolated latency misleading.
full_source_reviews.mechanism_and_state: Each DAG task selects CPU, immediate GPU or queued GPU. A runtime monitor owns measured load/VRAM/latency state; an LLM proposes placements and consumes feedback, while an algorithmic executor enforces dependency and memory feasibility.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: Nineteen profiled tools and thirteen constructed scenarios; comparisons with brute force, HEFT, UCB1, StarPU and all-GPU; mapping accuracy, end-to-end latency and convergence, including S13 ablation. The testbed, workload mix and prompt/model are bounded to the paper; production multi-tenant SLO and failure recovery are not established.
full_source_reviews.proved: The system reaches the brute-force-optimal mapping in all 13 reported scenarios and exposes cases where queueing or CPU placement beats immediate GPU use under contention/VRAM limits.
full_source_reviews.not_proved: It does not show that an LLM is required, generalization to unseen clusters, robustness to noisy telemetry, or superiority to trained/online optimizers at production scale.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_failure_coexistence: Language reasoning makes policy adaptation inspectable and zero-training but adds latency, nondeterminism and prompt sensitivity; the hard executor must retain authority. Static schedulers remain preferable for stable profiles, tight latency and well-modeled resources.

full_source_reviews.title: HiKV: Hierarchical Importance-Aware KV Cache with Hardware Acceleration for LLM Decoding

locators.artifact: Not Disclosed — exact v1 does not disclose a public executable HiKV artifact; evaluation claims remain limited to the paper's algorithm and modeled hardware contract

full_source_reviews.mechanism_summary: Hierarchical token and element selection exposes intra-token vector fetch as a second KV bandwidth floor and co-designs ranking state with a reconfigurable sorter.
full_source_reviews.analysis_old: Full KV is the exact baseline; token-only eviction is simpler and fits existing accelerators when retained-vector traffic is not dominant.
full_source_reviews.analysis_tradeoff: Two-granularity reduction adds approximation, offline calibration, fragmented accesses and specialized ranking hardware; commercial-GPU and production-SLO transfer are unproven.
full_source_reviews.problem_and_old_solution: Window/heuristic eviction is cheap but drops distant information; dynamic token importance improves quality but still loads every element of retained K/V vectors and pays recurring sorting cost.
full_source_reviews.mechanism_and_state: Stage I owns a recent bank plus frozen-importance bank maintained by a min-heap. Stage II selects dimensions/rows from Q and attention-probability magnitudes. A reconfigurable sorter time-multiplexes token- and element-ranking datapaths; compression ratios remain runtime configurable.
full_source_reviews.evaluation_contract: Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama3-8B, Mistral-7B and LongChat-7B across long-context/reasoning tasks; algorithm comparison under <=1% accuracy loss; accelerator post-layout at TSMC 16nm, 300MHz, 2.059 mm2, 135.4mW; system model reports memory traffic, speed and energy. Batch/concurrency and production SLO are not disclosed.
full_source_reviews.proved: Under the paper's iso-accuracy calibration, hierarchical selection averages 7.17x external-memory reduction and 5.70x modeled speedup, with 80-90% modeled energy reduction; the hierarchical support blocks occupy 8.64% area and 7.01% power of the proposed accelerator.
full_source_reviews.not_proved: The work does not establish equivalent gains on commercial GPUs, arbitrary workloads, dynamic per-request SLO budgets, or exact attention. Offline per-task calibration and modeled custom-hardware results constrain transfer.
full_source_reviews.tradeoff_failure_coexistence: Two granularities multiply bandwidth savings but introduce approximate attention, calibration, fragmented access and specialized silicon. Full KV remains the correctness baseline; token-only compression remains simpler where vector fetch is not dominant or custom hardware is unavailable.
